correctness.rationale: With d=n−1 tree edges, oriented incidence B has full rank and all n maximal minors ±1, whence det(BᵀB)=n. Each of the 2^d signed crosspolytope facets is a d−1 simplex and its pyramid with origin has intrinsic volume sqrt(n)/d!. Its supporting normal h_s satisfies Bᵀh_s=s and lies in 1⊥, so the facet area is sqrt(n)||h_s||/(d−1)!. Centered path potentials realize h_s, and ||h_s||²=(1/n)Σ_{u<v}(φ(u)−φ(v))². Rademacher independence gives E||h_s||²=W(T)/n and the claimed average squared area. Expanding E||Σ_e s_e q_e||⁴=a²+4Σ_{e<f}<q_e,q_f>²≤3a² and Hölder/Jensen proves sqrt(a/3)≤E||h||≤sqrt(a). On stars, ||h||²=n−1−Y²/n with Y a sum of n−1 signs, so ||h||/sqrt(n)→1 in probability and mean. On paths, a centered random walk scaled by sqrt(n) converges in C[0,1] to centered Brownian motion; the discrete L2 norm satisfies ||h||/n⇒sqrt(Q). Since E(||h||/n)²=(1−n⁻²)/6, uniform integrability gives expectation convergence. The mean-zero Neumann Green operator has eigenvalues 1/(π²k²), yielding Q=Σ Z_k²/(π²k²), and its Laplace product gives c=sqrt(2/π) ∫(1−sqrt(u/sinh u))/u²du. Independent direct incidence/facet Gram determinants for 16 tree cases (n=3..8, 744 signed facets) reproduce gram=n||h||² and exact Wiener means. Independent 60-digit quadrature gives c=0.3781319637260636570, as stated. Finite checks corroborate algebra only; analytic arguments establish arbitrary n and the limit.

Lattice equivalence preserves face structure and normalized volume, not intrinsic Euclidean facet measures; prior inradius max-norm, zonotope spherical width and balanced-simplex Wiener energy are different invariants. value.rationale: Every canonical n-vertex tree root polytope has the same combinatorial crosspolytope face lattice and intrinsic volume 2^(n−1)sqrt(n)/(n−1)!, making Euclidean boundary geometry a well-motivated invariant invisible to lattice equivalence. The exact squared-area moment converts its geometry into the Wiener index for every tree, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice. The path/star comparison exhibits qualitatively distinct typical facet areas (Brownian random profile versus deterministic concentration) and gives a nontrivial sharp sqrt(n) first-order surface ratio with an explicit universal constant. This is a useful complete structural identity plus an asymptotic classification of two canonical extremal tree families, without asserting unproved global extremality or an optimal universal lower bound.

final_claim: For the canonical Euclidean tree symmetric-edge polytope on n≥3 vertices, every facet is a signed-edge simplex, the uniform squared facet-area mean is W(T)/((n−2)!)², and total surface area is proportional to the expected L2 norm of the centered ±1 tree-potential. That expectation lies in [sqrt(W/(3n)),sqrt(W/n)]. Uniform star facet area normalized by n/(n−2)! converges in probability to 1, while uniform path facet area normalized by n^(3/2)/(n−2)! converges to sqrt(Q), with Q=∫(B−∫B)²=ΣZ_k²/(π²k²). Hence S_Path/S_Star ~ c sqrt(n), c=E sqrt(Q)=sqrt(2/pi)∫(1−sqrt(u/sinh u))/u²du=0.378131963726...; no global extremizer claim.
limitations: The claim is for unweighted finite trees with n≥3 embedded as the fixed ±(e_u−e_v) roots in H; unimodular coordinate changes are not Euclidean isometries.
The path/star ratio has an exact first-order constant only for those two families and is not a proof of path-maximizing or star-minimizing surface area over all trees.
The universal lower factor 1/sqrt(3) is not asserted optimal, and no convergence rates are proved.
Finite exact checks to n=8 and deterministic quadrature are corroborations, not proofs of infinite-order convergence or bibliographic priority.
